article.title: US Approves $2.68 Billion Military Sale to Ukraine for Air Defense Modernization
article.description: This Saturday, the U.S. State Department gave the green light for a potential $2.68 billion military sale to Ukraine, focusing on enhancing and expand...
paragraphs: Saturday, September 19, 2026 by Emily Vargas

This Saturday, the U.S. State Department gave the green light for a potential $2.68 billion military sale to Ukraine, focusing on enhancing and expanding its air defense capabilities against extensive Russian assaults.

The announcement was made by the U.S. Embassy in Kyiv via social media, highlighting that the deal aims to "augment Ukraine's ability to confront current and future threats, providing a more robust air defense for its self-defense missions and regional security."
Labeled as a potential Foreign Military Sale, the agreement is pending a review period by the U.S. Congress before it can be finalized.

The approved package comprises missile systems akin to the S-300 to replace outdated Soviet units still in use by Ukraine, GAM-67 missiles, long-range laser-guided rocket systems for air defense, and mobile launcher modification kits.

article.title: Israeli Forces Kill Four Palestinians, Including a Child, in Gaza
article.description: On Saturday, Israeli forces killed four Palestinians, including a child, and wounded several others in attacks across the besieged Gaza Strip, as Israel vio ...
paragraphs: On Saturday, Israeli forces killed four Palestinians, including a child, and wounded several others in attacks across the besieged Gaza Strip, as Israel violated the “ceasefire agreement” for the 345 th consecutive day.
Medical sources said an Israeli drone fired a missile at a vehicle in the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood, west of Gaza City, killing Yahia Hamdouna and wounding at least four other Palestinians.
Also, Bassir Monir al-Bعrsh , the son of Dr. Monir al-Barsh, director-general of the Palestinian Health Ministry, was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza.
In a separate attack, Raed Abu Aser was killed when the Israeli military bombarded Mushtaha Street in the Shuja’iyya neighborhood, east of Gaza City.

Elsewhere in Gaza City, Israeli tanks and artillery targeted the eastern part of the Tuffah neighborhood, while Israeli naval vessels fired shells offshore. Israeli forces also detonated and demolished buildings in northern Gaza.

article.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched 28 strikes in Yemen over 24 hours
paragraphs: The Houthis said Sunday that Saudi Arabia launched 28 strikes in several areas of Yemen in the past 24 hours, as the group and Yemeni government clash in the revived civil war.

“The Saudi air force carried out 28 strikes targeting the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, and Marib, using F-15 and Typhoon aircraft that took off from the Khamis Mushait and Taif airbases,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement.
This month, the Houthis launched an offensive to take over the country’s entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
The group insists that navigation of the strait is open and free except for Saudi vessels.

The United States reiterated its support for Yemen’s internationally recognised government on Wednesday as fighting intensified between the Saudi-led coalition and Houthi forces. US officials also held direct talks with Houthi representatives in Oman last weekend, according to sources cited by Reuters.

Yemeni government forces said that the coalition had struck Houthi positions around Mocha and that government forces had launched drone attacks in Marib. The Houthis claimed to have shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet over Marib.

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked regional and Western allies for help, according to two officials who spoke to The Associated Press news agency. The Saudis asked France, Pakistan, Egypt and the United Kingdom to deploy air-defence support to help defend against attacks by the Houthis. One official said Saudi Arabia’s main ally and arms supplier, the US, has seen its own stock of interceptors dwindle over the course of the war with Iran.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesman Tim Hawkins told Al Jazeera that the US is “closely monitoring” the situation between Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in Yemen, adding that the US military has a longstanding “military relationship with our Saudi partners, and you see that manifesting today”.

Even as Washington assists the Saudi campaign, American officials held direct talks with Houthi representatives in Oman last weekend, according to three sources who spoke to the Reuters news agency on condition of anonymity. The meeting took place at the US embassy in Muscat with the assistance of the Omani government, two of the sources said.

article.description: Houthi forces assert they have downed a Saudi armed reconnaissance drone in Yemens Marib province amid ongoing regional tensions.
paragraphs: Menu HOME HEADLINES UDAIPUR RAJASTHAN INDIA BUSINESS TECHNOLOGY ENTERTAINMENT SPORTS WORLD Houthi Rebels Claim to Shoot Down Saudi Drone in Yemens Marib 17 Sep 2026 11:47 AM by Ganpat Singh Chouhan Marib, September 17 (Udaipur Kiran) : Houthi rebels have announced that they successfully shot down an armed reconnaissance drone belonging to Saudi Arabia in the northeastern province of Marib, Yemen. The claim was made by Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sari during a statement aired on the Houthi-operated Al-Masirah TV on Wednesday evening.

Sari stated that the drone was targeted while flying over Marib and was brought down using appropriate weaponry. Earlier that day, the Houthis had also claimed to have downed a Saudi F-15 fighter jet, asserting that over 450 aerial attacks had been launched by Saudi forces on various districts in recent days.

According to Sari, the Houthi forces used locally manufactured surface-to-air missiles to intercept the Saudi fighter jet, which had entered Yemeni airspace over Mocha in western Taiz. He noted that the jets had taken off from the Khamis Mushait airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia.

The Houthi rebels have gained significant territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, recently capturing the strategic port city of Mocha on September 10, followed by the seizure of Mayyun Island located in the Bab al-Mandab strait, a crucial maritime route linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

The conflict in Yemen began in late 2014 when Houthi rebels took control of the capital, Sanaa, and large parts of northern Yemen. In March 2015, a Saudi-led coalition intervened in support of the internationally recognized Yemeni government.

article.title: Houthis claim 37 Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in 24 hrs
article.description: SANAA, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Yemen's Houthi group said on Thursday that Saudi Arabia's warplanes had carried out 37 airstrikes on two Yemeni provinces .....
paragraphs: SANAA, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Yemen's Houthi group said on Thursday that Saudi Arabia's warplanes had carried out 37 airstrikes on two Yemeni provinces over the past 24 hours, causing civilian casualties, as fighting between the Houthis and Yemen's government forces continued to intensify.

In a statement on social media platform X, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said Saudi F-15 fighter jets carried out the strikes in the southwestern province of Taiz and the northwestern province of Hajjah.
"Over the past 24 hours, Saudi warplanes carried out 37 airstrikes using F-15 aircraft that took off from Khamis Mushait Air Base," Sarea said, adding the strikes had killed and wounded civilians.
Sarea did not provide a detailed casualty toll.
There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities.

article.title: Saudi Arabia’s Oil Lifeline Just Went Down. The World May Be Out Of Time
article.description: Saudi Arabia could run out of oil available for export in days after an attack shut down a critical pipeline used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
paragraphs: My Account Read Politics US World Entertainment Sports Business Education Op-Eds Two Sides Big Tent Ideas Premium Content Newsletters Featured Partners Watch Inside CECOT Stream Documentaries Shop Premium Content Articles Documentaries Customer Support Subscribe Log In Energy Saudi Arabia’s Oil Lifeline Just Went Down. The World May Be Running Out Of Time (Photo by AFP via Getty Images)

Paris Apodaca Energy Reporter September 14, 2026 10:15 AM ET September 14, 2026 10:15 AM ET Paris Apodaca Energy Reporter Font Size: Saudi Arabia could run out of oil available for export within days after an attack shut down a critical pipeline used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The kingdom has enough crude stored at the Red Sea port of Yanbu to maintain current export levels for roughly five to seven days without new supplies flowing through its East-West Pipeline, Reuters reported Sunday citing Saudi oil buyers and traders. If the pipeline remains offline, the world risks losing as much as 4% of its oil supply. “This is a big outage for the Kingdom, and the damage to its East-West Pipeline appears much more severe than the relatively minor hit it took in April. Saudi storage farms in Egypt can fill in for the pipeline’s lost flows for perhaps a week, but a lingering shutdown beyond that would short global supply by about 4 million barrels per day,” energy public policy analyst David Blackmon told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

“Crude prices jumped 3% in overnight trading on the news, and U.S. gasoline prices will follow in the coming days. This incident, combined with lingering problems at the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, is likely to force gas prices at the pump even higher until they are favorably resolved,” Blackmon added.

The nearly 750-mile East-West Pipeline — owned by state-controlled oil company Saudi Aramco — was moving roughly four million barrels of crude per day toward Yanbu before an attack forced it offline, according to Reuters. Industry estimates for restoring the pipeline vary, with some sources telling the outlet repairs could take five to six weeks while others expect partial operations to resume sooner.

article.title: Yemeni forces clash with Houthis near Saudi border
article.description: Yemeni government forces clashed with Houthi fighters near the Saudi border, with AFP footage showing soldiers in armoured vehicles and trucks pushing across desert terrain under the crackle of machine-gun fire. The Houthis also released footage on Wednesday of the fighting in the northwestern Al-Jawf area, as well as a video purporting to show the downing of a fighter jet belonging to Saudi Arabia, the group's longtime foe and the Yemeni government's main backer.

The group has recently made major gains in a lightning offensive that Saudi airstrikes have failed to roll back, leaving the Yemeni government scrambling to respond.

The Houthis have been engaged in renewed fighting with Saudi-backed government forces since Yemen’s civil war reignited in July, when the group declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
The latest clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing Yemen’s Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Yayha Saree, the group’s military spokesman, said “the criminal Saudi enemy has carried out 58 airstrikes in the past 24 hours” in a post on Telegram.
